top.title: Today's Briefing
top.dek: The Rangers finally snapped the skid with a 3-1 win over the Blues, Tesla and SpaceX are sliding premarket after the midterms, and the Ocarina of Time remake reviews are in and glowing.

items.head: Skid over
items.text: Dylan Garand made 32 saves as the Rangers [beat the Blues 3-1](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxOUVRITFY2QUxwVXh2OFJpZlZOalN0WHVZYW1hUERoZGM5NmdLMTBjOTRBTDl5UGNCMHZmNUNVUU5Kcl8tTjYybFkxUmdQUmV3ZUE4bmN0YW5YZjVvOTVxcU1TelVSSmlQeWdJelc4R3ItTHpCM0w3ejFzSkNCaW9WeUdqYkZ4U0c1NjRJ?oc=5) to end four straight losses. Flyers at MSG **Thu Nov 5, 7 PM**.

items.head: Midterm hit for Musk stocks
items.text: **TSLA** and **SPCX** are [down about 4% premarket](https://news.google.?oc=5) after Democrats' big night, per CNBC.

items.head: Ocarina reviews drop
items.text: IGN [posted its review](https://x.com/IGN/status/2117934927140278611) calling the remake a beautiful retelling, and it's [topped Metacritic's 2026 list](https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-zelda-ocarina-of-time-remake-has-shot-to-the-top-of-metacritics-best-games-of-2026-so-far-makes-its-all-time-top-30/).

Yes, really.

items.text: 32 saves, a [3-1 win over St. Louis](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxOUVRITFY2QUxwVXh2OFJpZlZOalN0WHVZYW1hUERoZGM5NmdLMTBjOTRBTDl5UGNCMHZmNUNVUU5Kcl8tTjYybFkxUmdQUmV3ZUE4bmN0YW5YZjVvOTVxcU1TelVSSmlQeWdJelc4R3ItTHpCM0w3ejFzSkNCaW9WeUdqYkZ4U0c1NjRJ?oc=5), and the four-game skid is done. plans.html:
JJHC Varsity Practice — October 5, 2026

FieldValue
DateOctober 5, 2026
Ice8:00 PM–9:00 PM ET (60 min)
RinkIce Time Sports Complex, Newburgh NY
Shared withJunior Varsity
Focus themeControlled body contact & angling (night #1)
Roster~15 skaters + G Liam
Equipmentpucks, cones, tires/pads, whistle

ADM split target: ~50% skills / 30% hockey sense (SAG) / 20% systems.

Board cue: Angle first → stick second → body third. Heads up. No from-behind. Check to win the puck.

Goalie (Liam): Crease tracking during contact stations; no body-contact role. Soft shots from hashes when free; full compete in SAG.

Clock

MinBlockADM
0–8A. Warm-up + puck flowSkills
8–28B. Stations (3× ~6–7 min)Skills / Contact
28–42C. Small-area gameHockey sense
42–54D. Systems / teamSystems
54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Pit Chaos Handling with Passes

  • Directions: 2–4 players stickhandle inside a faceoff circle while 3–4 outside pass around the rim. Rotate every 20–30s. Heads up, find open ice, scan before the pass.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UxmQBKTJ2ss
  • Source: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/pit-chaos-handling-passes

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges; 5–8 Pit Chaos (both circles if numbers allow).

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — contact

1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill *(Hub Short)*

  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward forcing outside.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8
  • Source: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

Station 2 — contact / skills

Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence

  • Directions: Size-matched pairs. Side-by-side knees bent: 3 strides → shoulder/hip bump → continue; both directions. Lead with shoulder not head, elbows in, stick on ice. Half-speed first, then add a puck and board-side bumps.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jai0vHhRuEY
  • Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jai0vHhRuEY

Station 3 — skills / goalie

Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill

  • Directions: Receive in motion and shoot in one action. Emphasize catch-and-release and getting pucks through. Feed Liam quality looks from slot/hashes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978
  • Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978

Contact sprinkle: Angle Behind Net + Stick Check — O behind net, X angles to corner; stick lift/press or controlled rub only. Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw

C. Small-area game (28–42)

2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward *(Hub Short)*

  • Directions: Half-ice 2v2 with angling focus and a defensive reward after a takeaway. Continuous short shifts.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY
  • Source: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

Progression last 5 min: New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG (legal contact under tonight’s rules). Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY

D. Systems / team (42–54)

ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice; retrieval must go behind net before attacking; on turnover, F1 pressures. Reward attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY
  • Source: https://www.admkids.com/news_article/show/754281-10u-18u-f1-forecheck-game

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill *(Hub Short)*

  • Directions: 1v1 race to dumped puck, then layer to 3v3 transition as support arrives.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI
  • Source: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

Last 2 min: easy skate; repeat board cue. Optional 60s leadership clip: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/wwOIUxHVMTw

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Pit Chaos Handling with Passes* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill*) → no-goalie: 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 1v1 in a faceoff circle; carry the puck out through any of three gates, roles flip on a turnover. Keeps tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Station 2: *Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill*. Two lines, alternate sides; one shot + one rebound per rep and the next shooter only goes when Liam is set (~15–20 s). Cap it at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie). Net angled in the corner, dividers box the area; 2v2, 45-s shifts, keep score. Tonight's constraint: defender must angle first, stick second, body third — legal contact only; a clean angle-and-pin that wins the puck = 1 point. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward*? Already half-ice to one net — keep it on Liam's net; the defensive reward stays a clear/outlet pass to the coach, so no second net is needed.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free The Gate Game (no goalie); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)* → Cross-ice 3v3 to one net: the forecheck team attacks Liam; the retrieving team must skate behind Liam's net and then score by hitting a tire at the far end. The F1 pressure rule stays. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey). 2v2 on one net with Liam as neutral goalie; after every change of possession the puck must go below the goal line before attacking. Theme rule: on every possession change the new defender closes on an angle before the puck reaches the goal line. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill* → The race and the 3v3 attack Liam's net; on a change of possession the new team must complete a pass to the coach at the blue line (that's the 'transition') before attacking the same net. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: No shot while a contact battle is still in the crease; pucks low and from the slot only, and Liam calls 'time' if bodies land on him.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Engage Goalies at Practice (USA Hockey). USA Hockey: warm the goalie first, quality over quantity, and let him hop out for a few reps in high-volume drills.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

JJHC Varsity Practice — October 7, 2026

FieldValue
DateOctober 7, 2026
Ice8:45 PM–9:45 PM ET (60 min)
RinkMcCann Ice Arena, Poughkeepsie NY
Shared withJunior Varsity
Focus themeSkating edges, gaps & retrievals
Roster~15 skaters + G Liam
Equipmentpucks, cones, tires/pads, whistle

ADM split target: ~50% skills / 30% hockey sense (SAG) / 20% systems.

Board cue: Eyes up. Stick on ice. Move after every pass.

Goalie (Liam): Primary shot volume at Stations 1–2 (the 3v3 and race-to-3v3 nets) and the scoring blocks. Station 3 (Pit Chaos) has no net. Call for catch-and-release quality.

Clock

MinBlockADM
0–8A. Warm-up + puck flowSkills
8–28B. Stations (3× ~6–7 min)Skills / Contact
28–42C. Small-area gameHockey sense
42–54D. Systems / teamSystems
54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Ice Hockey Passing Drill - Rondo Progressions

  • Directions: Rondo-style passing progressions (keep-away circles). Start with more attackers than defenders and shrink the outlet time. Cue one-touch options and body shape to receive.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JW2BBDdR07I

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — sag|skills

3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM

  • Directions: Full-team 3v3 play-fast small-area game. Keep all lines rotating with short shifts so nobody stands. Emphasize first touch, immediate support, and transition the instant possession changes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg

Station 2 — contact|sag

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

Station 3 — warm-up|skills

Pit Chaos Handling with Passes

  • Directions: The Pit Chaos Handling With Passing drill is an excellent activity that helps players work on awareness, puck handling, and passing skills. This drill can be used as a warm-up in practice or games, or as a drill to reinforce keeping your head up. Setup Setup 2, 3, or 4 players in the middle of a face-off circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UxmQBKTJ2ss

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward

  • Directions: Half-ice 2v2 with angling focus and a defensive reward rule (e.g., clear/score after a takeaway). Offense must move to support; defense angles first, then stick, then body. Continuous short shifts so everyone gets reps.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY

C. Small-area game (28–42)

2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill

  • Directions: 2-on-1 that uses the net as a pick/screen and deception tool. Offense delays, uses the net to change sides, and looks for the late attacker; defender manages gap and stick while protecting the middle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6ioQDMwYlw

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game

  • Directions: Two nets back-to-back (or close). Teams attack opposite directions in a tight area, battling for possession and quick shots. High compete, high shot volume for the goalie when one net is live.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k6WXVVGkfTo

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Skating edges, gaps & retrievals). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Ice Hockey Passing Drill - Rondo Progressions* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM*) → no-goalie: Transition Pivot Races. Head-to-head pivot race (forward–backward–forward) finishing in a race to a coach-placed puck; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (Skating edges, gaps & retrievals) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill*. The race and the 3v3 attack Liam's net; on a change of possession the new team must complete a pass to the coach at the blue line (that's the 'transition') before attacking the same net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *Pit Chaos Handling with Passes* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 3 on 2 Race to 5 (Cail MacLean). Below the circles, 3 F vs 2 D + Liam; F goal = 1, D skate it past the line = 1, Liam freeze = 1; first to 5. Tonight's constraint: every dump is a retrieval race — shoulder-check before the puck, tight turn away from pressure, first pass within two touches. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp*? One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill* → Every rush goes into Liam's end; alternate start corners and send one 2-on-1 every ~20 s so he can set and track the late attacker. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Horseshoe Regroup 2-on-1 (one goalie). Shot + rebound, then a D-to-D regroup that turns into a 2-on-1 back into Liam's same net (the step-up D must recover his gap). Theme rule: grade the step-up D on his gap — he must be back inside the dots before the 2-on-1 crosses the blue line. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game* → Liam covers BOTH back-to-back nets (Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters) format) — or turn one net toward the boards and count only shots that hit a tire set in its mouth. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots come in stride off the retrieval only — no stop-and-blast; one shot max per retrieval rep.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Engage Goalies at Practice (USA Hockey). USA Hockey: warm the goalie first, quality over quantity, and let him hop out for a few reps in high-volume drills.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

The game also creates opportunities to work on re-entry rush offense as players transition between offensive and defensive roles. 2 rush with an additional backchecking player, creating a 2 vs.

E. Finisher (54–60): *Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game* → Liam covers BOTH back-to-back nets (Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters) format) — or turn one net toward the boards and count only shots that hit a tire set in its mouth. Station 2 — goalie|skills

  • Directions: Goalie edgework and shuffles that do not require a painted crease—use cones or boards. Pair with skater stations so Liam gets focused movement work while others rotate.

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game

Board cue: Short shifts, support the puck, make the 2-on-1 — attack, pass, go to the net.

Teams: 5 groups of 3 (pinnies). 3v3 = 2 groups play, 1 waits on the bench line and jumps in on the whistle. 4v3 = add a 4th "joker" attacker who always plays offense. Shifts 30–40 s, change on the fly.

Goalie (Liam): In the net for every game at his end; second goalie (if present) takes the other end. Coach restarts only when he's set.

Clock

MinBlockADM

41–51E. 3v3 Blast Off rush (zone entries)Systems
51–60F. Medicine Hat 3v3 finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–5)

4 Dot Quick Warmup

  • Directions: Lines at the four end-zone dots; skate, pass, and receive in motion around the dots, then a quick shot. Keep everyone moving — no lines longer than 3.
  • Cues: heads up, give a target, pass to space.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hpq3DYJ1IeU (HockeyShare)

B. Cross-ice 3v3 (5–17)

Cross-Ice 3v3 Game

  • Directions: Zone split into cross-ice rinks (net at each boards side). 3v3, 30–40 s shifts on the whistle; waiting group jumps in, tired group off. Puck dead → coach spots a new one immediately.
  • Cues: always a support option, move after you pass, first to the puck wins.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Vxk7V3HXvA (Evolution Hockey)

C. 4v3 breakout game (17–29)

4v3 Breakout Game

  • Directions: Coach dumps in; 4 attackers (3 + joker) break out vs 3 forecheckers, then attack back into the zone. Light theme: once over the line, look to create a 2-on-1 on the weak side.
  • Cues: talk early, use the extra man, attack the D's inside foot, drive the far post.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rk5x2QYYmtk (Hockey Coach Vision)

D. 3v3 Royal Road (29–41)

3v3 Royal Road Small Area Game

  • Directions: 3v3 in the zone; a goal counts only (or counts double) if the puck crosses the "royal road" (middle line through the slot) before the shot. Short shifts, change on the fly.
  • Cues: move the goalie side to side, find the open stick, D take away the middle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KVALab3nGHI (HockeyShare)

E. 3v3 Blast Off rush (41–51)

3vs3 Blast Off

  • Directions: 3 attackers vs 3 backcheckers released from the neutral zone; attack the zone with speed — carry in, drive wide, or chip. Quick walkthrough (<1 min), then live.
  • Cues: gain the line with speed, middle lane drives, late man fills high slot.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xgZ_AAL1xdk (The Coaches Site)

F. Finisher + cool-down (51–60)

Medicine Hat 3v3

  • Directions: Compete 3v3 in the zone, 30 s shifts, team scores → stays on. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch.
  • Cues: win battles, protect the puck, shoot through traffic.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BhwSW95zfao (Hockey Coach Vision)

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Same clock. Far net: pull to boards with tires on the goal line (tire targets) or skip and use one net.

  • B (5–17): Cross-ice 3v3 at Liam's end only; the other cross-ice rink becomes 3v3 + Perimeter Options on tire targets (perimeter outlet players keep everyone involved).
  • C (17–29): 4v3 breakout attacks Liam's net only; on a whistle every ~25 s.
  • D (29–41): Swap to 3 v 3 Corner Hockey Game — one net, battles start in the corner.
  • E (41–51): If rushes bog down, run Revolving 2 on 1 on Liam's net — continuous, light 2-on-1 theme.
  • F (51–60): Medicine Hat 3v3 as written on one net.

Liam's workload: ~40 of 60 min in net. Breaks: 0–3 own crease warm-up · 17–18 and 29–30 block transitions · 41–42 walkthrough on empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Tap-out rule: late on two lateral pushes → hops out 3–4 reps, skaters finish on tire target. No point bombs.

ADM self-check

  • Every skater touching the puck every shift (3v3/4v3, 5 groups of 3)
  • Shifts ≤ 40 s, transitions < 60 s
  • Body contact / battles present
  • Liam got quality game-like looks

54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence

  • Directions: Size-matched pairs. Side-by-side knees bent: 3 strides → shoulder/hip bump → continue; both directions. Lead with shoulder not head, elbows in, stick on ice. Half-speed first, then add a puck and board-side bumps. Contact every practice.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — contact|skills

1 v 1 Use The Net

  • Directions: 1 v 1 Use the Net from Jason Lammers is a great drill for all age levels that encourages offensive awareness and puck protection while the defenders work on angling and proper stick detail. The offensive team is trying to skate the puck through the gate while the defender is looking to strip the puck and score on net. Setup Setup a net and a gate as the goals.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1154377465

Station 2 — sag|goalie|skills

2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game

  • Directions: 2v2 battle off rebound looks. Coach or shooter creates a rebound; both pairs compete for second chances and net-front body position. Excellent goalie tracking volume.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I

Station 3 — skills|goalie

Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill

  • Directions: Offensive-zone timing drill: receive in motion and shoot in one action. Emphasize catch-and-release, weight transfer, and getting the puck through from tough angles. Feed Liam quality looks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Perry Pearn Tracking Game

  • Directions: Objective The Perry Pearn Tracking Game from John Dean helps teams develop the habit of tracking through the puck at a 45-degree angle after possession is lost. The offensive team works together to prevent exits, extend zone time, and wear down defenders until pressure creates a turnover or scoring opportunity. 3 below an imaginary line connecting the tops of the circles.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1229638212

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game

  • Directions: 3v3 version of Gates of Buffalo. Teams score by completing passes through cone/tire gates while moving to open ice. Progress by shrinking gates or adding a defender.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adueXqyfyNs

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

3 on 3 Add a D

  • Directions: This small-area game emphasizes encouraging your defense to join the rush while working on quick transitions, support, puck movement, and recognizing when to activate the extra player. Setup Shorten the rink by placing each net at the tops of the circles. Teams line up 3 on 3 in the neutral zone.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1137930754

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game

  • Directions: Cross-ice 3v2 that rewards quick east-west play and late support. Defense manages middle ice and sticks in lanes; offense looks for the third attacker.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (F1 forecheck & tracking). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*1 v 1 Use The Net*) → no-goalie: Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game. 1v1 in the middle with wall support; carry it across outside the cones = 1 pt, through the middle gate = 2 pts; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (F1 forecheck & tracking) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Station 2 (*2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game*) → no-goalie: 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 1v1 in a faceoff circle; carry the puck out through any of three gates, roles flip on a turnover. Keeps tonight's focus (F1 forecheck & tracking) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill*. Two lines, alternate sides; one shot + one rebound per rep and the next shooter only goes when Liam is set (~15–20 s). Cap it at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (Perry Pearn Tracking Game)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game. Half a zone, 3 F vs 3 D on Liam's net; goal = 2 pts, D complete a pass and exit = 1 pt. Tonight's constraint: pressure team: F1 must reach the puck carrier within 2 s of the goalie deflection; F2 takes the pass option. ▶ video

  • *Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game* is already goalie-free, so keeping it as written is fine; use the one-net game above when you want Liam in the SAG block.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *3 on 3 Add a D* → Keep Liam's net; replace the other net with two tires. The team going toward the tires must hit its activated D with a pass before it can score on a tire. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 3 on 2 Race to 5 (Cail MacLean). Below the circles, 3 F vs 2 D + Liam; F goal = 1, D skate it past the line = 1, Liam freeze = 1; first to 5. Theme rule: forwards score double on a goal created by an F1 turnover. ▶ video (IHS page)

E. Finisher (54–60): *Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game* → Liam in one cross-ice net; the defenders' counterattack scores by hitting a tire where the second net was. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots only after a forecheck turnover, from below the tops of the circles — quality over volume.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

plans.html:
JJHC Varsity Practice — November 2, 2026

FieldValue
DateMon Nov 2, 2026
Ice7:15–8:15 PM ET (60 min)
RinkMcCann Ice Arena, Poughkeepsie NY
Shared withJunior Varsity
Focus themeGet it in, get it out, heads up, stay disciplined through contact
ContextFri L 6-3 OCW (fell apart in 3rd on penalties); Sun T 1-1 Washingtonville. Joey sore after a late hit Fri.
Roster~15 skaters + G Liam
Equipmentpucks, cones, tires, pinnies (light/dark)

ADM split: ~40% skills/contact · 40% small-area games · 20% systems.

Board cue: Heads up before the puck. Absorb, protect, move it. Hands down, stick down, no retaliation — we don't go down a man.

Discipline rule (all night): any stick infraction, retaliation, or hit from behind = that team plays a man down for the next shift. Coach calls it out loud.

Joey: if still sore, non-contact jersey for Station 1 and contact reps; full go in everything else.

Clock

MinBlockADM
0–6A. Warm-up (heads up)Skills
6–24B. Stations (3× 6 min): contact / protectionSkills / Contact
24–36C. SAG: 4v3 Breakout (exits)Hockey sense
36–48D. 3v3 Blast Off (entries)Systems / sense
48–58E. Medicine Hat 3v3 (discipline compete)Compete
58–60F. Cool-down + board cue—

A. Warm-up (0–6) — 4 Dot Quick Warmup

  • Setup: lines at all four NZ dots with pucks, skate through the middle on the whistle.
  • Cues: chin up through traffic, call names, no looking at the puck. Liam takes soft shots last minute.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hpq3DYJ1IeU

B. Stations (6–24) — 3 groups, 6 min each

Station 1 — 2 Player Partner Bump Open Ice (absorbing contact)

  • Setup: size-matched pairs, 3 strides, shoulder/hip bump both sides; half speed → 3/4 → add a puck.
  • Cues: knees bent, wide base, elbows in, head up and out of the boards' line, absorb with the legs then skate out of it. Never turn your back to the hit.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jai0vHhRuEY

Station 2 — Finders Keepers (puck protection)

  • Setup: tight circle, carriers protect, chasers steal; 20–30 s reps.
  • Cues: body between man and puck, low center, hands away from pressure, eyes up to find an outlet.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=veI7-0o8n5o

Station 3 — 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (on Liam)

  • Setup: coach dumps into corner, 2v2 below the dots, one net.
  • Cues: protect along the wall, legal body position only, stick down = no hooks/slashes. Win it, get it to the slot.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V97nywNK4lo

C. SAG (24–36) — 4v3 Breakout Game (exits)

  • Setup: coach dumps in; 4 (incl. D) break out vs 3 forecheckers; exit = controlled carry or pass over the blue line, then attack back in.
  • Cues: D shoulder-check before the puck, strong-side wall support, middle option, chip it off the glass if pressured. No blind rims.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rk5x2QYYmtk

D. Rush game (36–48) — 3vs3 Blast Off (entries)

  • Setup: 3v3 rush from the neutral zone into one end, groups go on the whistle.
  • Cues: carry with speed wide, middle drive, late man; if no lane, chip and chase to a spot — no turnovers at the blue line.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xgZ_AAL1xdk

E. Finisher (48–58) — Medicine Hat 3v3

  • Setup: scoring team stays on, 30–40 s shifts, light vs dark.
  • Discipline rule live: an infraction = man down next shift. Take the hit to make the play, then get up and skate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BhwSW95zfao

F. Cool-down (58–60)

Easy laps, stretch, repeat the board cue. Quick word on Friday's 3rd period: stay five on the ice.

One-goalie option (Liam only; Kerry doesn't practice)

  • A: No change; Liam self-warm-up 0–4, then soft shots.
  • B: Stations 1 and 2 need no goalie. Station 3 stays on Liam, coach-fed, ~12 shots/rotation, break around 15:00.
  • C: All 4v3 attacks finish on Liam's net. If it bogs down, run 3 v 3 Corner Hockey Game at the far end on tires.
  • D: Blast Off rushes go to Liam's end only; between reps, the waiting group plays 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (no net).
  • E: Medicine Hat on one net; or 3 Small Area Games w/ 1 or 0 Goalies.
  • Workload: ~40 min in net; breaks 0–4, ~15:00, 24–26 walkthrough, 36–38, 58–60. Two soft goals in a row = he sits 3–4 reps.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact taught and practiced safely
  • Entries and exits both got live reps
  • Discipline rule called every time
  • Liam got quality looks
  • Transitions < 60 s

plans.html:
JJHC Varsity Practice — November 4, 2026

FieldValue
DateWed Nov 4, 2026
Ice8:45–9:45 PM ET (60 min)
RinkMcCann Ice Arena, Poughkeepsie NY
Shared withJunior Varsity
Focus themeExits under pressure, entries with speed, heads up, stay five-on-five
ContextBuilds on Monday (Nov 2). Fri L 6-3 OCW (penalties in the 3rd); Sun T 1-1 Washingtonville. Joey sore after a late hit Fri.
Roster~15 skaters + G Liam
Equipmentpucks, cones, tires, pinnies (light/dark)

ADM split: ~40% skills/contact · 40% small-area games · 20% systems. New drills from Monday, same arc.

Board cue: Heads up before the puck. Take the hit, make the play. Exit with a purpose, enter with speed, never dump it blind. Stick down, no retaliation, stay five.

Discipline rule (all night): any stick infraction, retaliation, or hit from behind = that team plays a man down for the next shift. Coach calls it out loud.

Joey: if still sore, non-contact jersey for Station 1 and Station 2 (stick-only defending, no body contact on him); full go in the games otherwise.

Clock

MinBlockADM
0–6A. Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up (heads up, call names)Skills
6–24B. Stations (3× 6 min): angle / contain / net-frontSkills / Contact
24–36C. Nowak Transition Game, 4v3 (exits)Hockey sense
36–48D. Chip n Chase SAG (entries)Systems / sense
48–58E. 3 on 3 Play Fast (discipline compete)Compete

A. Warm-up (0–6) — Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up

  • Setup: full-team flow, five pucks moving at once; skaters pass and receive while skating through traffic.
  • Cues: chin up, call for it by name, receive on the move. Liam takes soft shots in the last minute.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IsD9ZDgPO0k

B. Stations (6–24) — 3 groups, 6 min each

Station 1 — 1v1 Angle Game Behind Net (giving and taking contact on the wall)

  • Setup: carrier goes behind the net; defender angles to the wall and finishes with stick lift or a controlled rub. Switch roles every rep.
  • Cues: carrier: wide base, protect with the body, absorb on the boards and skate out of it. Defender: angle first, stick second, body third. Nothing from behind and no numbers showing.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw

Station 2 — 2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Game with Defensive Reward (win it and get out)

  • Setup: 2v2 half-ice. Defenders who win the puck score by making a clean exit pass or carry through a gate at the blue line.
  • Cues: win it with legal body position, then shoulder-check and move it. Hands down, stick down.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PfpCL35u1tY

Station 3 — 2v2 Block Out Battle (on Liam)

  • Setup: coach shot from the point, 2v2 net-front battle for the rebound.
  • Cues: box out with the body, stick on the ice; no cross-checks, no slashes after the whistle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NwE0EoveHBM

C. SAG (24–36) — Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game, 4v3 (exits)

  • Setup: two zones, no goalie. Coach dumps in; the team of 4 (incl. D) retrieves and exits through a blue-line gate against 3 forecheckers. A clean exit scores, then the team attacks the far gate. On a turnover, the other team transitions.
  • Cues: shoulder-check before you touch it, wall support, middle option, chip it off the glass if pressured. No blind rims up the middle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cc1xg7o1weo

D. Rush game (36–48) — Chip n Chase Small Area Game (entries)

  • Setup: 3v3. Attackers enter by carrying in with speed or by chipping to space behind the D and winning the race. A goal counts only after a clean entry.
  • Cues: speed wide, middle drive, late man. Chip to a spot, not to the goalie. A turnover at the blue line gives the other team the puck right away.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mUFHMpRuXN0

E. Finisher (48–58) — 3 on 3 Play Fast Small Area Game

  • Setup: 3v3, 30–40 s shifts, light vs dark, everyone rotates in.
  • Discipline rule live: an infraction = man down next shift. Take the hit, make the play, get up and skate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE

F. Cool-down (58–60)

Easy laps, stretch, repeat the board cue. Quick word: two practices now on staying five on the ice. Bring it Friday.

One-goalie option (Liam only; Kerry doesn't practice)

  • A: Liam does his own warm-up 0–4, then soft shots. Option: Shooting Recovery Drill with two shooters in the last 2 min.
  • B: Stations 1 and 2 need no goalie. Station 3 stays on Liam, coach-fed, ~10–12 shots per rotation. Break around 15:00.
  • C: The Nowak game needs no goalie, so Liam rests 24–36 except for the last ~4 min, when exits finish with a shot on him. If the game bogs down, use The Gate Game at the far end.
  • D: Chip n Chase finishes on Liam's net only. The waiting group plays Cross-Ice 3v3 on tires at the far end.
  • E: 3 on 3 Play Fast on one net, or 2 Small Area Games w/ 1 Goalie.
  • Workload: ~40 min in net. Breaks at 0–4, ~15:00, 24–32 and 58–60. Two soft goals in a row = he sits 3–4 reps.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact taught and practiced safely (angle, absorb, box out)
  • Exits and entries both got live reps
  • Discipline rule called every time

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!

  • Directions: Open practice with a 12-player SAG so everyone is active immediately. Use a half-zone or below-dots box, short shifts, and a simple scoring rule. Sets tempo and compete early.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vtqsH0Zw8I

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — skills|sag

3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey

  • Directions: 3v1 keep-away to train support, deception, and defensive stick positioning. On turnover or after a time limit, flip roles. Progress to 3v2.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x6epwQk1POE

Station 2 — sag|systems

3 on 3 Add a D

  • Directions: This small-area game emphasizes encouraging your defense to join the rush while working on quick transitions, support, puck movement, and recognizing when to activate the extra player. Setup Shorten the rink by placing each net at the tops of the circles. Teams line up 3 on 3 in the neutral zone.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1137930754

Station 3 — warm-up|skills

Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team

  • Directions: Full-team warm-up with five pucks moving. Players keep circulating, exchanging passes, and filling lanes so the ice stays alive. Great openers for touch, awareness, and tempo before stations.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IsD9ZDgPO0k

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game

  • Directions: Cross-ice 3v2 that rewards quick east-west play and late support. Defense manages middle ice and sticks in lanes; offense looks for the third attacker.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Perry Pearn Tracking Game

  • Directions: Objective The Perry Pearn Tracking Game from John Dean helps teams develop the habit of tracking through the puck at a 45-degree angle after possession is lost. The offensive team works together to prevent exits, extend zone time, and wear down defenders until pressure creates a turnover or scoring opportunity. 3 below an imaginary line connecting the tops of the circles.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1229638212

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game

  • Directions: The major concept of the Gates of Buffalo Small Area Hockey Game is to practice moving to open space, communicating verbally and non-verbally with teammates, so they can score Goals by passing through Gates.   • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JlKKAFlVTLc

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Special-teams habits (PP entry / PK pressure)). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. A. Warm-up (0–8): *Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!*: Play it to tire targets (two tires per end) instead of nets — no goalie needed. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *3 on 3 Add a D*. Keep Liam's net; replace the other net with two tires. The team going toward the tires must hit its activated D with a pass before it can score on a tire. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking))*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Sticks In Lanes Game (Topher Scott). 6 fixed attackers vs 2 defenders in the middle, one net; 2+ passes through the middle before a shot; sticks on the ice. Tonight's constraint: PP side needs 2 passes through the middle before a shot; PK sticks on the ice or the coach awards a penalty shot. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game*? Liam in one cross-ice net; the defenders' counterattack scores by hitting a tire where the second net was.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Perry Pearn Tracking Game* → Play it in Liam's zone; the defending team's controlled exit over the blue line counts as their goal, so no second net is needed. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Power Play Scoring Competition (Wes Wolfe). 60-s PP rounds on Liam: 5-on-0 entry, then one PKer added every 15 s up to 5-on-4; most goals wins. Theme rule: each PP unit gets three 60-s rounds; PK scores by icing it. ▶ video (IHS page)

E. Finisher (54–60): *Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game* is goalie-free — run as written; Liam does 2 minutes of easy lateral movement and stretches in the crease.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: PP one-timers only after 2+ passes; whistle after each goal or freeze so he resets.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward the defender for forcing outside and the attacker for protecting the puck through contact.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

Station 3 — sag|skills

Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1

  • Directions: The Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1 is an excellent small area game for all age levels that helps players practice a 2 vs 1 in a small space along the boards in the corner of the ice. The game reinforces important skills like keeping your head up, moving to open spaces, protecting the puck, and verbal & non-verbal communication. Offensive players should practice using the boards to make bank passes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hnLu_shT2J0

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

C. Small-area game (28–42)

3 on 3 Add a D

  • Directions: This small-area game emphasizes encouraging your defense to join the rush while working on quick transitions, support, puck movement, and recognizing when to activate the extra player. Setup Shorten the rink by placing each net at the tops of the circles. Teams line up 3 on 3 in the neutral zone.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1137930754

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/784999967

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Oreo

  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/847506383

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Middle-ice deny & stick detail). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers. His shuffles/edgework from Station 1 move here.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*Practice Goalie Shuffles & Edgework with No Crease*) → skater no-goalie station: 2vs2 Shooting Board Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 2v2 net-front game with shooting boards (no goalie); defenders stay goal-side, cut lanes, play the body. Keeps tonight's focus (Middle-ice deny & stick detail) while Liam does his edgework in the warm-up instead. ▶ video
  • Station 2 (*1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill*) → no-goalie: Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies). Keep-away inside a faceoff circle (2v1 → 3v1 → 4v2 monkey-in-the-middle); no goalie needed. Keeps tonight's focus (Middle-ice deny & stick detail) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1*. Already low-volume on one net — keep it on Liam's net and finish each rep with one shot only. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Sticks In Lanes Game (Topher Scott). 6 fixed attackers vs 2 defenders in the middle, one net; 2+ passes through the middle before a shot; sticks on the ice. Tonight's constraint: defenders score a point for every intercepted middle pass; sticks never leave the ice. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *3 on 3 Add a D*? Keep Liam's net; replace the other net with two tires. The team going toward the tires must hit its activated D with a pass before it can score on a tire.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free 2vs2 Shooting Board Game (IIHF Skills4Life); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush* → One direction only, into Liam's end; the next pair leaves when Liam is set, and the D come back up the wall as their rest. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Gretzky 3 vs 2 Behind the Net. Below the circle tops, one net; team of 3 must always keep a forward below the goal line, D talk through the switches. Theme rule: defenders protect the slot first — goals from the middle cost double. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Oreo* → Keep it on Liam's net (offense scores, defense outlets to the next line); cap shifts at 30 s so the shot count stays sane. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots only through a lane the offense earned; no point blasts through a forest of sticks.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Station 1 — contact|skills

1 v 1 Use The Net

  • Directions: 1 v 1 Use the Net from Jason Lammers is a great drill for all age levels that encourages offensive awareness and puck protection while the defenders work on angling and proper stick detail. Station 2 — sag|goalie|skills

Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game

This game framework will help players learn to play with their head up, communicate with teammates and move to open space. As a coach, If you commit to working on activities like this instead of memorization drills for a portion of each practice, you will marvel at how your team begins to work together.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JlKKAFlVTLc

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward

Swap in Half Ice Shoot In Stride — Two lines alternate: call for the coach's pass, shoot in stride before the cone, stop at the net for a rebound.
  • Station 3: *Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Swiss 4 vs 2 Scoring Game. Zone split high/low into two 2v1s on Liam's net (4 v 2); defenders stay in their area, shot within ~5 s. Tonight's constraint: shot must come off the first touch after a pass (catch-and-release), inside 5 s. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1*? Already low-volume on one net — keep it on Liam's net and finish each rep with one shot only.

E. Finisher (54–60): *Ramsay 3 V 3 Race* → The race decides offense; offense attacks Liam. If the defenders win the puck they score by carrying it through a cone gate at the tops of the circles. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.

  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Ride The Bull

  • Directions: Objective Ride The Bull is a small area game from Matt Thomas that works on developing puck protection and possession skills under pressure. Teams must protect the puck, use their teammates, and keep possession for 8 seconds. If they are able to accomplish this, they are awarded a 3rd teammate and each teams begin game play to try to score on the opposing teams net.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1228177222

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward*) → no-goalie: Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game. 1v1 in the middle with wall support; carry it across outside the cones = 1 pt, through the middle gate = 2 pts; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *Bentley Wall Cycling Drill*. Already a one-net half-ice drill — keep it on Liam's net and alternate sides every rep so shots come from both walls. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3 (*Oreo*) → no-goalie: 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 1v1 in a faceoff circle; carry the puck out through any of three gates, roles flip on a turnover. Keeps tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey). 2v2 on one net with Liam as neutral goalie; after every change of possession the puck must go below the goal line before attacking. Tonight's constraint: defender must take the inside lane with stick on puck before any body contact; coach awards a point for a controlled rub-out on the wall. ▶ video

  • *Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game* is already goalie-free, so keeping it as written is fine; use the one-net game above when you want Liam in the SAG block.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (IIHF Skills4Life); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)* → Attack only toward Liam's net; when the backcheckers win the puck they 'score' by passing to their partners waiting in the small neutral zone. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 3 on 2 Race to 5 (Cail MacLean). Below the circles, 3 F vs 2 D + Liam; F goal = 1, D skate it past the line = 1, Liam freeze = 1; first to 5. Theme rule: D earn their point only after angling the carrier into the wall first. ▶ video (IHS page)

E. Finisher (54–60): *Ride The Bull* → The keep-possession phase needs no net; when a team earns its third player it attacks Liam's net. Runs to one net as written. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: No shot while a contact battle is still in the crease; pucks low and from the slot only, and Liam calls 'time' if bodies land on him.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

  • Station 1: *Corner Tires - Small Area Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game*. Run as written on Liam's net, but the coach controls the feed: one shot, play the rebound out, new puck only when Liam is set. Cap at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled. Prefer more finishing looks? Swap in Half Ice Shoot In Stride — Two lines alternate: call for the coach's pass, shoot in stride before the cone, stop at the net for a rebound.
  • Station 3 (*Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game*) → no-goalie: 2vs2 Shooting Board Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 2v2 net-front game with shooting boards (no goalie); defenders stay goal-side, cut lanes, play the body.   • *Contact sprinkle (1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position)* — no net needed; unchanged.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

Coach shot off Liam's pads → forwards crash, D box out; next whistle forwards race the cones and a second puck starts 2v2 down low. Tonight's constraint: the first rebound is the only coach shot — everything after is a live 2v2; D win = clear it to the corner. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *Ramsay 3 V 3 Race*? The race decides offense; offense attacks Liam. If the defenders win the puck they score by carrying it through a cone gate at the tops of the circles.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Tire Deke & Shoot Station; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *What it means to be a good leader with Gold Medalist Hayley Scamurra* needs no net — run it, then use the remaining minutes for Tomas Holmstrom SAG (net-front): Box from the dots to the circle tops; 3 O vs 2 D fight for net-front while a shooter fires 5 pucks (one per whistle); attackers tag up outside the box every whistle. Theme rule: defenders get a point for every shot they block or every attacker they keep outside the box. ▶ video (IHS page)

E. Finisher (54–60): *ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)* → Cross-ice 3v3 to one net: the forecheck team attacks Liam; the retrieving team must skate behind Liam's net and then score by hitting a tire at the far end. The F1 pressure rule stays. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Screens and tips are the point, but it's one shot per rep and a reset whistle after every rebound — no point slappers into traffic.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

  • *Contact sprinkle (Puck Race to Possession Game)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.

Tonight's constraint: the first forward to the dump is F1 and must angle the D to one side; goals off a forecheck turnover count double. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)*? Cross-ice with Liam in one net; the other net is replaced by two tires — a 'goal' there is hitting a tire after a pass.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game. Half a zone, 3 F vs 3 D on Liam's net; goal = 2 pts, D complete a pass and exit = 1 pt. Theme rule: forwards track back through the middle after every D exit. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward* → Already half-ice to one net — keep it on Liam's net; the defensive reward stays a clear/outlet pass to the coach, so no second net is needed. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

MinBlockADM

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players

  • Directions: Warm-up flow that links retrievals to first-pass exits. Skaters retrieve, hit a support target, and transition up ice without standing still. Great for D breakout habits.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WIgVxM39sZE

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — contact|systems

Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/784999967

Station 2 — sag|skills

Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)

  • Directions: This is a phenomenal drill in several ways. First, the concept of this drill can be used in many different areas of the ice. Secondly, it forces players to think 2 on 1's in tight spaces.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/342763238

Station 3 — sag|skills

Ramsay 3 V 3 Race

  • Directions: Jason Lammers describes the Ramsay 3 V 3 Race. This competitive small area game incorporates racing to the puck to determine which team is on offense. Setup Full ice setup with goalies in both nets.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/861028778

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

C. Small-area game (28–42)

USA Activation Drill (14U+)

  • Directions: Coach shoots a puck across; first two from each line race to it while the next two become activating D behind the nets. Possession side can attack or kick back to activating D for a 4v2. Run 30-second shifts; teach battle + activate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Bentley Wall Cycling Drill

  • Directions: This drill helps players work on their wall play and cycling under pressure. SETUP: This is a half ice drill, there should be a net in its usual spot on the goal line. There should be a line of players starting on one of the dots with a pile of pucks.

  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

  • Station 3 (*Ramsay 3 V 3 Race*) → no-goalie: 2vs2 Shooting Board Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 2v2 net-front game with shooting boards (no goalie); defenders stay goal-side, cut lanes, play the body. Keeps tonight's focus (Compete night — SAGs & battles) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *USA Activation Drill (14U+)*? The possession side attacks Liam (or kicks it back to the activating D); if the other side wins it, they score by hitting a tire at the far dot after a D-to-D pass.

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.

  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Station 3 — warm-up|skills

  • Directions: The Pit Chaos Handling With Passing drill is an excellent activity that helps players work on awareness, puck handling, and passing skills. Station 2 — contact|sag

42–54D. Systems / teamSystems
54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Pit Chaos Handling with Passes

  • Directions: The Pit Chaos Handling With Passing drill is an excellent activity that helps players work on awareness, puck handling, and passing skills. This drill can be used as a warm-up in practice or games, or as a drill to reinforce keeping your head up. Setup Setup 2, 3, or 4 players in the middle of a face-off circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UxmQBKTJ2ss

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — contact|sag

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

Station 2 — skills|systems

Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill

  • Directions: 2-on-1 that uses the net as a pick/screen and deception tool. Offense delays, uses the net to change sides, and looks for the late attacker; defender manages gap and stick while protecting the middle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6ioQDMwYlw

Station 3 — sag|goalie|skills

2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game

  • Directions: 2v2 battle off rebound looks. Coach or shooter creates a rebound; both pairs compete for second chances and net-front body position. Excellent goalie tracking volume.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game

  • Directions: 3v3 version of Gates of Buffalo. Teams score by completing passes through cone/tire gates while moving to open ice. Progress by shrinking gates or adding a defender.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adueXqyfyNs

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/784999967

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!

  • Directions: Open practice with a 12-player SAG so everyone is active immediately. Use a half-zone or below-dots box, short shifts, and a simple scoring rule. Sets tempo and compete early.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vtqsH0Zw8I

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull the far-end net to the boards and set two tires on the goal line (tire targets). If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Pit Chaos Handling with Passes* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill*) → no-goalie: 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 1v1 in a faceoff circle; carry the puck out through any of three gates, roles flip on a turnover. Keeps tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Station 2 (*Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill*) → no-goalie: Transition Pivot Races. Head-to-head pivot race (forward–backward–forward) finishing in a race to a coach-placed puck; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game*. Run as written on Liam's net, but the coach controls the feed: one shot, play the rebound out, new puck only when Liam is set. Cap at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets). Cross-ice; one team shoots on Liam, the other scores by hitting 2 tires at the far end; flip ends every time the tire team scores. Tonight's constraint: the tire team may only start its attack after winning the puck with an angle + stick (no lunging); illegal contact = possession to the other team. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • *Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game* is already goalie-free, so keeping it as written is fine; use the one-net game above when you want Liam in the SAG block.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush* → One direction only, into Liam's end; the next pair leaves when Liam is set, and the D come back up the wall as their rest. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie). Net angled in the corner, dividers box the area; 2v2, 45-s shifts, keep score. Theme rule: 45-s shifts; contact is controlled rub-outs only — count angle-and-pin wins. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!* → Play it to tire targets (two tires per end) instead of nets — no goalie needed. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: No shot while a contact battle is still in the crease; pucks low and from the slot only, and Liam calls 'time' if bodies land on him.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds
